name: Living Hell
label: Revelation
lede: Members of three dead New England hardcore bands started Living Hell in 2007. Their demo got pressed by two labels, then Revelation put out The Lost and the Damned, which ends in more than five minutes of static.

eras.title: Three dead bands, one dark one
eras.text: Living Hell grew out of Dead Wrong, Fear Tomorrow and Follow Through, and pointed at the bleak, metallic Cleveland sound of Integrity. Within a year of forming they had gone from a demo to a Revelation LP.

years.h: Dead Wrong, Fear Tomorrow and Follow Through become Living Hell
years.p: Craig Mack sings, Seann McKay and Dan Sullivan play guitar, Jim Volinski plays bass and Jack LaBarca drums. Revelation lists them as coming from "all corners of New England."

yt: Parable of a Madman, from the demo
years.h: A five-song demo gets pressed twice
years.p: Rock Vegas puts the demo out on CD, and Lockin' Out Records presses it as a red 7", Pavor Nocturnis.
years.xp:
The EP opens the way the band meant to go on: Parable of the Mad Man is one of its five songs. Discogs dates the Lockin' Out 7" to 2007.

A389 Recordings later put the same five songs up digitally, billed as Integrity-inspired hardcore.

years.src: Scene Point Blank · Punknews · Revelation Records: pressing history · Bandcamp
years.h: Revelation REV 145 puts out the full album
years.p: Twelve songs, The Resurrection to King of Kings. Scene Point Blank gave The Lost and the Damned 9 out of 10.
years.xp:
Reviewers heard Integrity everywhere. Scene Point Blank caught Dwid in Mack's darker delivery and the Systems Overload vibe in Condemned; Punknews said Mack was "achingly similar to Jamey Jasta" of [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]].

Punknews called it metallic hardcore "leaning more on the core," with breakdowns kept short, and picked Drawn to Chaos, Mask of Sanity and Condemned as repeat listens, each under 90 seconds.

Revelation's first vinyl run was 330 on grey and white, 326 on opaque red, and a second press of 110 on black.

years.p: That's how Punknews describes the end of King of Kings, the last track on The Lost and the Damned. The reviewer said it swamped the three minutes of music before it.
